If the cell's byte 2 is 0xFF, returns 2 (off-map). Otherwise cell byte 3 is an attribute index into TWO SEPARATE tables sharing one idx=attr*4: Data_0202c000[idx]'s low nibble selects a ROM function-pointer table at 0x080134fc, and the ADDRESS of Data_0202c001[idx] is passed as that function's first argument alongside the position's own low-4-bit x/z fractions -- an indirect call through the r3 call-via-rN veneer slot (0x080072f0). That height minus object->height is compared against +0x80000 (too high -> return 1) and -0xC0000 (too big a drop -> return -1), else returns 0 (passable).

One real structural correction found and applied this session: the inherited draft modelled the per-attribute record as a single `struct TerrainAttrRecord { u8 kind; u8 data; ... }` array (attr_addr+1 for the second field), which only accounts for the 0x0202c000 literal. The retained assembly (games/gs1/asm/080120dc.s) actually pools THREE distinct 4-byte constants -- 0x03001e70, 0x02010000, 0x0202c000, 0x080134fc, 0x0202c001, 0xfff40000 -- and its instruction stream loads 0x0202c000 and 0x0202c001 as two INDEPENDENT bases (two separate `ldr rX,[pc,#N]` loads, both later added to the same attr_idx*4 register), not one struct base plus a +1 byte offset. Replacing the struct with two parallel `extern u8 Data_0202c000[]; extern u8 Data_0202c001[];` arrays sharing one `idx = cell[3] << 2` correctly reproduces both literals and the shared-index reuse pattern. differing_halfwords stayed at 72 (dominated by the register-allocation residual below), but this is a strictly more evidence-backed model -- the struct model is provably wrong since it cannot emit the 0x0202c001 constant that the reference genuinely contains -- so it replaces the inherited draft rather than being kept alongside it.

Tried and rejected as a further lead: an explicit intermediate `u8 *entry = &Data_0202c000[idx]; kind = *entry;` to force the reference's separate address-then-load-at-offset-0 pattern (vs. one fused register-indexed ldrb). The compiler folds this back to a single indexed load regardless of the intermediate pointer variable or a re-derived (non-CSE'd) `attr_idx << 2` computed twice -- this compiler's forward-substitution is not source-structure-sensitive here, so it is not a usable lever without an escape hatch.

Remaining residual (all ~72 differing halfwords) is a single coherent register-allocation hunk, confirmed by inspecting every '!' line in the aligned diff: every mismatch is a same-mnemonic, same-immediate operand rename, never a differing opcode. The reference keeps THREE persistent callee-saved locals live across the whole body and the indirect call (x in r5, z in r6, object in r7 -- push/pop {r5,r6,r7,lr}), while this compiler's allocator only commits two (z and object) and keeps x in caller-saved r4 (push/pop {r5,r6,lr}), an 8-byte-shorter, leaf-adjacent allocation. All three locals have an identical use-count/live-range shape (one def, two uses spanning the same code region: x and z are each read once for tile flooring and once for the final &15 mask; object is read once for map_layer and once post-call for height) -- confirmed by an explicit register-by-register use count over the retained .s -- so this is not explainable by a source-visible liveness or use-count difference; it is the allocator's internal tie-break for which of three equally-live pseudo-registers gets the last callee-saved slot. This matches the same 'final register-letter/allocation choice not controllable via source reordering' floor already catalogued elsewhere in this corpus (see e.g. 080fb2a4.json's leaf-vs-framed residual). Not eligible for permanent-assembly classification (no compiler-pass evidence that the shape is unreachable, only that this session's source-level search did not find the lever); retained assembly stays authoritative and this draft claims zero DONE bytes.
